stem:
> “Despite campaigning against big government, the Reagan administration presided over rising federal deficits, as tax cuts and a defense buildup outpaced the spending cuts it achieved.”
>
> *Source: A historian, early twenty-first century*

Which of the following best supports the historian's argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Iran-Contra affair was investigated by Congress and by an independent special prosecutor.
choices.explanation: That concerns a scandal, not budget policy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Moral Majority mobilized evangelical voters around issues such as abortion and school prayer.
choices.explanation: That concerns political mobilization.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The 1981 tax cuts and large increases in military spending coincided with growing deficits.
choices.explanation: Lower revenue and higher defense spending contributed to larger deficits.

choices.label: D
choices.text: President Reagan fired striking air traffic controllers in 1981 and weakened organized labor.
choices.explanation: That concerned labor relations, not the deficit.

explanation: Tax cuts and defense spending increases coincided with growing deficits.

stem: The Republican victory in the 1994 midterm elections, associated with the Contract with America,

choices.label: A
choices.text: led to the impeachment of President Reagan for his role in the Iran-Contra scandal.
choices.explanation: Reagan had left office in 1989.

choices.label: B
choices.text: gave Republicans control of both houses of Congress for the first time in decades.
choices.explanation: The election was a major shift in congressional power.

choices.label: C
choices.text: ended the two-party system when independent candidates won control of both houses.
choices.explanation: The system continued.

choices.label: D
choices.text: gave Democrats a larger majority in the House and Senate, supporting Clinton's agenda.
choices.explanation: Republicans gained control.

explanation: The 1994 elections shifted control of Congress to the Republicans.

stem: President Bill Clinton's approach as a New Democrat is best illustrated by

choices.label: A
choices.text: a call to expand the Great Society programs without change and raise taxes on the middle class.
choices.explanation: Clinton moved away from traditional liberalism.

choices.label: B
choices.text: his opposition to all free trade agreements and his strong support for higher tariffs.
choices.explanation: He supported NAFTA.

choices.label: C
choices.text: his proposal to abolish the income tax and replace it with a national sales tax on goods.
choices.explanation: Clinton did not propose that.

choices.label: D
choices.text: backing NAFTA, welfare reform and balanced budgets, which moved Democrats toward the center.
choices.explanation: Clinton adopted policies that appealed to moderates.

explanation: Clinton's centrist policies included NAFTA and welfare reform.

stem:
> “Scholars disagree about why the Cold War ended. Some emphasize the pressure of American military spending and firm rhetoric; others argue that the internal weaknesses of the Soviet system and the reforms of Mikhail Gorbachev were decisive.”
>
> *Source: A historian, early twenty-first century*

Which of the following best supports the second view described in the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The United States proposed the Strategic Defense Initiative in 1983 to defend against missiles.
choices.explanation: That supports the view stressing American pressure.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Soviet economy stagnated, and Gorbachev's reforms unleashed forces he could not control.
choices.explanation: Internal economic weakness and the effects of reform are the heart of the second view.

choices.label: C
choices.text: NATO admitted several new members from Eastern Europe in the late 1990s and 2000s.
choices.explanation: That occurred after the Cold War ended.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The United States increased defense spending in the early 1980s to pressure the Soviet economy.
choices.explanation: That also supports the first view.

explanation: Soviet internal problems and Gorbachev's reforms support the second view.

stem: The expansion of NATO in the 1990s to include former Warsaw Pact states

choices.label: A
choices.text: was opposed by every Eastern European government and by many Western European allies.
choices.explanation: Many Eastern European governments sought membership.

choices.label: B
choices.text: extended NATO eastward, which backers said secured democracy and critics said provoked Russia.
choices.explanation: The expansion was controversial in Russia and in the West.

choices.label: C
choices.text: ended NATO as an organization once the Warsaw Pact had dissolved in 1991 and its members left.
choices.explanation: NATO continued and grew.

choices.label: D
choices.text: was a Soviet-led initiative meant to preserve Moscow's influence over its former allies.
choices.explanation: The Soviet Union no longer existed.

explanation: NATO's expansion eastward was supported by many but criticized by others.

stem: President George H. W. Bush ended the Gulf War after liberating Kuwait rather than invading Iraq because

choices.label: A
choices.text: the coalition's mission was limited to freeing Kuwait, and he feared a long occupation.
choices.explanation: The administration wanted to keep the war's goals limited and the coalition united.

choices.label: B
choices.text: American forces had been defeated by Iraqi troops and had to withdraw from the region.
choices.explanation: The coalition had won a decisive victory.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Congress had declared the war illegal and ordered the president to end it at once.
choices.explanation: Congress had authorized force.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the Soviet Union threatened to invade if the coalition advanced toward Baghdad.
choices.explanation: That was not the reason.

explanation: Limited goals and coalition concerns led to the end of the war.

stem:
> “Globalization lowered prices for consumers and created new export industries, but it also contributed to the decline of American manufacturing communities.”
>
> *Source: A historian, early twenty-first century*

Which of the following best supports the second part of the historian's claim?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Midwestern factory closings and lost jobs as production moved overseas and to Mexico.
choices.explanation: The loss of factory jobs in particular regions illustrates the decline of manufacturing communities.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The rise of the Silicon Valley technology industry and its high-paying jobs in California.
choices.explanation: That reflects growth in one region, not decline elsewhere.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The growth of the Internet in the 1990s and the rise of online commerce and retail.
choices.explanation: That concerns technology rather than the decline of manufacturing communities.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The expansion of cheap imported goods in stores and discount retail chains nationwide.
choices.explanation: That supports the claim about lower prices for consumers.

explanation: Factory closings in Midwestern communities show the decline of manufacturing.

stem: The dot-com boom and bust of the late 1990s and early 2000s

choices.label: A
choices.text: occurred during the Great Depression and caused a wave of bank failures across the nation.
choices.explanation: It occurred decades later.

choices.label: B
choices.text: led to the end of personal computers as consumers turned instead to mobile phones.
choices.explanation: Computers continued to spread.

choices.label: C
choices.text: reflected speculative investment in Internet companies that failed when the bubble burst.
choices.explanation: Overinvestment led to a market crash but did not end technological change.

choices.label: D
choices.text: showed that the Internet had no lasting commercial value and would never be profitable.
choices.explanation: The Internet continued to grow.

explanation: The dot-com bubble burst, yet the Internet continued to transform the economy.

stem: The Dodd-Frank Act of 2010 sought to

choices.label: A
choices.text: tighten financial regulation and create the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.
choices.explanation: The law aimed to reduce the risk of another financial crisis.

choices.label: B
choices.text: create the Social Security system, with pensions for retired and disabled workers.
choices.explanation: Social Security was created in 1935.

choices.label: C
choices.text: abolish the Federal Reserve and return control of banking to the individual states.
choices.explanation: The Federal Reserve remained.

choices.label: D
choices.text: end all regulation of banks and let the market alone govern all lending practices.
choices.explanation: The law increased regulation.

explanation: Dodd-Frank expanded financial regulation after the 2008 crisis.

stem:
> “After 2001, presidents of both parties asserted broad executive authority in national security matters, often without explicit new approval from Congress.”
>
> *Source: A historian, early twenty-first century*

Which of the following best supports the historian's argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Department of Homeland Security was created in 2002 to coordinate dozens of security agencies.
choices.explanation: That shows institutional change but not an assertion of executive authority beyond congressional approval.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Congress's 2001 military authorization was cited for years to justify action against terrorist groups.
choices.explanation: A single authorization was used to support a widening set of actions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Congress passed the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution in 1964, authorizing force in Vietnam without a declaration.
choices.explanation: That occurred decades earlier.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The United States joined the United Nations in 1945 and helped write its charter in San Francisco.
choices.explanation: That occurred long before 2001.

explanation: The 2001 authorization was used to justify broad executive action.

stem: Which of the following best describes the aftermath of the 2003 invasion of Iraq?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The discovery of large stockpiles of chemical weapons and an active program to build nuclear arms.
choices.explanation: Such stockpiles were not found.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Saddam Hussein's fall was followed by a long insurgency and sectarian violence that eroded public support.
choices.explanation: The occupation proved long and costly.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An immediate withdrawal of American forces within months of Saddam Hussein's capture in 2003.
choices.explanation: American forces remained for years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A quick, peaceful transition to a stable democracy within a year or two of the invasion.
choices.explanation: Violence continued for years.

explanation: A prolonged insurgency and violence followed the invasion.

stem: The Arab Spring of 2011 presented United States policymakers with

choices.label: A
choices.text: a united Middle East aligned with Soviet power and opposed to the Western democracies.
choices.explanation: The Soviet Union no longer existed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: a simple choice to support every government in the region against the protest movements.
choices.explanation: Responses varied by country.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the challenge of responding to uprisings against authoritarian governments, some allies.
choices.explanation: American leaders had to balance support for democratic aspirations with alliances.

choices.label: D
choices.text: an end to American involvement in the region once the uprisings had spread to many states.
choices.explanation: American involvement continued.

explanation: The Arab Spring raised difficult questions about supporting allies and democracy.

stem:
> “Our state spends millions on services for people who entered the country illegally. The voters are saying enough. We must end public benefits for those here illegally.”
>
> *Source: A governor's statement, 1994*

The passage best reflects which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Growing political conflict over immigration, as in California's Proposition 187.
choices.explanation: The statement reflects efforts to restrict benefits for undocumented immigrants.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Support for the Immigration Act of 1965 and its rules for family reunification.
choices.explanation: The statement reflects a restrictive position.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A call for open borders and a pathway to citizenship for every resident.
choices.explanation: The statement calls for restrictions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The expansion of the Great Society and its programs for immigrants and poor families.
choices.explanation: The statement calls for ending benefits.

explanation: The passage reflects the immigration debates of the 1990s.

stem: The Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program of 2012

choices.label: A
choices.text: let some immigrants who arrived as children stay and work temporarily, without citizenship.
choices.explanation: The program offered temporary protection, not permanent status.

choices.label: B
choices.text: granted citizenship to all undocumented immigrants who had lived in the country five years.
choices.explanation: It did not provide citizenship.

choices.label: C
choices.text: was passed as a constitutional amendment and ratified by three-fourths of the states in 2012.
choices.explanation: It was an executive action.

choices.label: D
choices.text: ended all deportations of undocumented immigrants and closed the nation's immigration courts.
choices.explanation: It applied to a limited group.

explanation: DACA offered temporary relief without citizenship.

stem: Which developments reflect the expansion of legal recognition of LGBTQ rights between 2003 and 2015?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lawrence v. Texas (2003), the repeal of Don't Ask, Don't Tell (2010) and Obergefell (2015).
choices.explanation: These events ended criminal penalties, allowed open military service and recognized same-sex marriage.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Plessy v. Ferguson (1896), the Taft-Hartley Act (1947) and Roe v. Wade (1973).
choices.explanation: These concern other issues and time periods.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Chinese Exclusion Act (1882), the Dawes Act (1887) and the Sherman Act (1890).
choices.explanation: These are nineteenth-century laws.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Voting Rights Act of 1965 and the creation of Medicare.
choices.explanation: These are 1960s laws and are not about LGBTQ rights.

explanation: Lawrence, the repeal of Don't Ask, Don't Tell and Obergefell expanded LGBTQ rights.
